header.note_en: Written 45 + oral 5 = 50 marks. The oral part is taken by the teacher from the marking scheme.
header.note_ur: تحریری 45 + زبانی 5 = 50 نمبر۔ زبانی حصہ استاد مارکنگ اسکیم سے لیں گے۔

slots.prompt_rule: Five rows of four or five numbers in order up to 100, each with one blank (__) to fill. Answer: the missing number.
Five series (count on by 1, 2, 5 or 10, or count back by 1) with two blanks each; 1 mark per blank. Answer: both numbers.

Five items, each a picture of 1 to 10 of one book object (picture: {kind:"count", name, n}) or dots ({kind:"dots", n}). The instruction asks the question; the item needs no stem. Answer: n. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.
Five pairs of numbers up to 100 written "34 ☐ 43". Answer: the sign.

sections.note_en: Teacher: the teacher reads each story in Q5 and Q6 aloud, twice; the child listens and writes the working.

slots.instruction_en: Listen to the story and solve. Show your working.
slots.prompt_rule: Five one-step addition stories from the book, sums up to 20; each story is one sentence of at most 10 words with one name, one object and numbers up to 20, never two-part stories (morning and evening); each story ends with its question ("How many ... now?"), never facts alone; the teacher reads each story aloud, so the child hears it rather than reads it. Answer: the number sentence and the sum. The key pays the number: any correct working earns it (a number sentence, counting or a drawing); never write "writes the number sentence" or the unit as a requirement, the paper only says "Show your working". One rule: a correct answer with no working still earns the mark (the key says so in its accept line).

slots.instruction_en: Listen to the story and solve. Show your working.
slots.prompt_rule: Five one-step take-away stories from the book, numbers up to 20; each story is one sentence of at most 10 words with one name and one object, never two-part stories; each story ends with its question ("How many ... are left?"), never facts alone; the teacher reads each story aloud. Answer: the number sentence and the difference. The key pays the number: any correct working earns it (a number sentence, counting or a drawing); never write "writes the number sentence" or the unit as a requirement, the paper only says "Show your working". One rule: a correct answer with no working still earns the mark (the key says so in its accept line).

slots.instruction_en: Write the name of each shape.
slots.prompt_rule: Five items, each one shape the book teaches (circle, square, triangle, rectangle, oval, star, heart) drawn as picture: {kind:"shapes", shapes:[{shape}]}. The item needs no stem. Answer: the name. Never the same shape twice. The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

Five compare items from the book's measurement pages (longer/shorter, taller/shorter, heavier/lighter, more/less). Each carries picture: {kind:"scene", describe} naming two objects of different kinds side by side that lie straight, standing or lying on one base line with a gap between them, never one above, under or overlapping the other; the two objects differ by at least double in the compared measure and the picture draws that difference plainly; heavier/lighter pairs are ones every Grade 1 child knows without the picture (a brick and a feather, an elephant and a mouse), never judged from drawn size; e.g. "a pencil and a crayon"; never two of the same thing; never ribbon, rope, string or anything that curls. Stem asks which is longer/heavier etc. Name each object with one plain word a Grade 1 child can say and spell (pencil, crayon, bus, motorbike, brick, feather, elephant, mouse), the same word in the describe and in the answer, never a made-up or two-word brand name. Only objects a 6-year-old names one way, drawn plainly (bus, pencil, crayon, elephant, mouse, tree, flower, brick as a red wall brick with its pattern of lines, never a plain grey block that could be an eraser or a box); the child writes the name, so the key lists the usual other names in accept (`scheme.accept`: block for brick, bike or motorcycle for motorbike). Answer: the object, named as in the describe and without a size word ("the pencil", never "the long pencil"). The picture is a plain black-outline drawing a child names at once: never a thing whose outline alone is unreadable (egg, ball, plate, cup, watch, bench, box). A small object placed in a scene is drawn large and in front.

lines_en: One mark per correct item unless the paper says otherwise. Spelling is not marked unless the key says so.
Written marks only. Record the oral marks from the oral sheet, then add both on the class record.
lines_ur: جب تک پرچے میں کچھ اور نہ لکھا ہو، ہر درست جواب پر 1 نمبر۔ املا کے نمبر صرف وہاں کٹتے ہیں جہاں کلید میں لکھا ہو۔
یہ صرف تحریری نمبر ہیں۔ زبانی نمبر زبانی جائزے کی شیٹ سے لکھیں، پھر کلاس ریکارڈ پر دونوں جمع کریں۔

lines_en: This is the marking scheme for {file} ({n} pages). Do not give it to children.
Photocopy the question paper, all {n} pages, one per child.
You add: {duty} on the question paper, page {p} (book p. {b}).
Mark question by question across all copies, not copy by copy.
lines_ur: یہ {file} ({n} صفحات) کی مارکنگ اسکیم ہے۔ بچوں کو نہ دیں۔
سوالیہ پرچے کے تمام {n} صفحات کی فوٹو کاپی کریں، ہر بچے کے لیے ایک۔
شامل کریں: {duty}، سوالیہ پرچہ صفحہ {p} (کتاب ص {b})۔
ہر سوال کو تمام کاپیوں میں ایک ساتھ جانچیں، ایک کاپی مکمل کر کے دوسری نہیں۔

oral.note_en: Take the oral part after the written paper, one child at a time. Read the script aloud as written.
oral.note_ur: زبانی حصہ تحریری پرچے کے بعد، ہر بچے سے الگ الگ لیں۔ اسکرپٹ لکھے ہوئے الفاظ میں پڑھ کر سنائیں۔

tasks.instruction_en: Ask each question aloud once. The child answers aloud; no paper or fingers counted against them.
tasks.instruction_ur: ہر سوال ایک بار بلند آواز سے پوچھیں۔ بچہ زبانی جواب دے۔
tasks.ask: Five quick questions read aloud: count on, one more/one less, add or take away within 10, which number is bigger. Each with its answer. An item's script has no number other than the one(s) it asks about: no story with other counts (never "three flowers, four birds" before "count on from 4").
